items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: if you ever have heard of him, was the first black trumpet player that played jazz in the style.

ctx.x: Yeah? I didn’t know that. I thought Benny Goodman was one of the first guys with — so that’s an interesting fact.
Yeah, a lot of people didn’t pay much attention to that in those days. Because it wasn’t obvious. But those were good old days and as you say, Johnny Dunn, if you ever have © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

heard of him, was the first black trumpet player that played jazz in the style. Now he moved up from, I’ll start in New Orleans. New Orleans is where it started. You know I mean jazz, I’m not talking about the Africans that came over with the drums, I’m talking about the horn players. It started in Louisiana. I was there. I went all through everything they had there.

items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: The first recording that I heard was Johnny Dunn. A trumpet player.

ctx.x: In the '20's, did you listen -- there wasn't too much jazz on the radio, but did you listen to a lot of records?
Yes, oh, yes. Oh yes. The first recording that I heard was Johnny Dunn. A trumpet player.
